facts.F255: S5 open-host narrowing keeps the property route (option A), with one owner: ModuleRules owns the set-up boundary. ModuleRules holds SetUpContracts, the positive pattern of Organisation set-up's Contracts namespace built from ContextContractsMembership.ContractsOf("OrganisationSetup"), and SetUpBehindItsContracts, the negative pattern derived from the same name; both are properties, not constants, so the namespace-move law does not read them as rule patterns. Every downstream rule reuses them: WorkItems' SetUpOpenToTheContextsBuildingOnIt becomes ModuleRules.SetUpContracts (or is removed and its readers use it), the composites in Promises (TheNamespacedUpstreamCodeAndSetUpBehindItsContracts) and Refinement (TheForbiddenCodeAndSetUpBehindItsContracts) and the Access, Licensing, Reports and WorkItems layer patterns compose ModuleRules.SetUpBehindItsContracts, and OrganisationSetupIsAnOpenHostArchUnitTest's open list uses ContextContractsMembership.ContractsOf("OrganisationSetup") instead of SetUpModule + ".Contracts". The declared pattern roles (ContextContractsPatternRoles, OrganisationSetupPatternRoles) stay unchanged: they describe what the namespace-move law sees, not the open host, and moving the narrowing there would put a boundary owner inside the move law. Option B rejected for that reason.
